
  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  lsof — List Open Files & Network Sockets
  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  On Unix, network sockets are files — lsof doubles as a network diagnostic
  tool. Essential for finding what's using a port.

  ▸ Port Diagnostics
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lsof -i :3000                   Show all processes using port 3000
  Shows PID, process name, user, socket state (LISTEN/CLOSED/etc)
  lsof -ti :3000                  PIDs only (terse) — pipe into kill
    -t                            Terse output: only PIDs, no headers
    -i :PORT                      Filter to network connections on PORT
  lsof -i :3000 -sTCP:LISTEN      Only actively LISTENING processes
  Filters out stale CLOSED sockets — use this to check if a port is free
    -sTCP:LISTEN                  Filter by TCP socket state
  lsof -i :3000,:3001,:5432       Check multiple ports at once

  ▸ Kill Processes on a Port
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lsof -ti :3000 | xargs kill     Graceful kill (SIGTERM)
  -t gives bare PIDs which pipe cleanly into kill
  lsof -ti :3000 | xargs kill -9  Force kill (SIGKILL)
  Use for zombie processes that survive SIGTERM

  ▸ System Overview
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lsof -i -P | grep LISTEN        All listening ports on the machine
    -P                            Show port numbers (not service names)
  lsof -p 12345                   All files/sockets open by PID 12345
  Useful for debugging what a specific process is doing
  lsof -i -P -n                   All network connections (fast, no DNS lookup)
    -n                            Skip DNS resolution — much faster

  ▸ Flag Reference
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    -i [proto][@host][:port]      Filter by network address
    -t                            Terse: PIDs only, no header — for piping
    -P                            Port numbers instead of service names
    -n                            No DNS resolution (faster)
    -p <PID>                      Filter to specific process ID
    -sTCP:STATE                   Filter by TCP state (LISTEN, ESTABLISHED,
                                  CLOSED)
    -c <name>                     Filter by process name
    +D <dir>                      All open files under a directory (recursive)
